conditions.reasoning: The decision is a closed set of three branches. Each branch names its condition, the permitted action, and whether the workflow continues and whether the official result is produced — the candidate is if anything more explicit about result production than the reference, which leaves it to the `Passed | Stopped` union. The loop limit is stated with its exit conditions immediately above the branches it governs. The open-ended-looking 'unless the person who asked for the task agrees to more' is not an undeclared escape: branch three declares the ask, declares that continuation requires a yes, and declares what happens on a no. A separate derivation rule closes the gap between review statuses and the branch conditions ('Anything a review does not record as done or passing is outstanding'), which is the same job the reference does through its pass/fail verdict types. I can articulate no form difference here.

structures.reasoning: The subagent device is used well and in the right places — four `Subagent: Role (→ `Type`)` declarations, parallel work announced before the two subagents that perform it, domain types defined in the types file rather than described in the body. But the frontmatter contract is incomplete and the types file drops the reference's chief declarative device. The reference declares a workspace in frontmatter and names it in the body; the candidate declares none anywhere. The reference declares its input as a domain type defined in contracts.py; the candidate inlines a primitive annotation in frontmatter and defines no input type at all. And the reference encodes determinacy structurally through discriminated unions, so a passed report cannot carry issues; the candidate's flat models push that guarantee back into prose.

coverage.reasoning: One responsibility the reference carries is dropped outright, and three the source carried but the reference deliberately compressed away are retained. Dropped: the workspace — the reference makes it a frontmatter declaration, requires a fresh one per execution, adds a scoping note that the workspace does not confine task effects, and reports it at the end; the candidate has no persistent artifact trail at all. Retained past the reference's line: verbatim task propagation (source's 'verbatim task from task.md' — the reference simply says 'complete the user's task'); user permission to exceed the cap (source's 'Max 5 iterations without user permission' — the reference makes the cap a hard stop); and 'don't redo passing work' (source's Fixer instruction 2). The candidate also keeps the source's three-state outcome verdict (`concern`) that the reference collapsed to pass/fail, and does not carry the reference's constraint that a fix hint be used only when evidence-supported and root-cause-addressing. The loop would behave observably differently from the reference at the cap and would leave nothing on disk to inspect.

what_to_fix_in_the_sculpting_skill: The sculpting skill has no reconciliation step that forces an explicit drop-or-declare decision on each of the source's side effects and guardrails. Add a rule with two halves. First: every artifact the source persists (workspace, run directory, per-iteration reports, status logs) must be resolved into exactly one frontmatter declaration — a workspace or output field — or consciously dropped; it may not simply evaporate because the mechanics were deleted. The candidate deleted the source's log and directory mechanics correctly but took the workspace responsibility down with them, losing the frontmatter workspace field the reference retains. Second: every guardrail bullet in the source must be re-derived from the sculpted flow rather than carried over — keep it only if the flow would be underdetermined without it. That rule would have caught the verbatim-task sentence, the 'leave passing work untouched' clause, and the negotiable cap, all three of which are source guardrails that survived because they are individually defensible by pointing back at the source.
